tags.name: Dakit-Dakit
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: reclassified pinnacle->reef. Three independent operator/guide sites (Evolution Diving Resort, Malapascua Thresher Shark Divers, Diverbliss) describe this as a shallow boulder/reef site (8-15m), not a freestanding pinnacle. Difficulty corrected Intermediate->Beginner to match consensus (shallow, easy site).

tags.name: Ka-Osting / Bantigue
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: reclassified reef->muck. Three operator sources independently describe Bantigue/Ka-Osting (aka East Garden) as a shallow-reef-to-sand muck site (12-18m), not a coral reef. Depth corrected from 22m to 18m max to match sourced range.

tags.name: Evo House Reef
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: reclassified reef->muck; this is Evolution Diving Resort's own house reef, consistently described by 3 independent sources as one of the region's best muck/macro dives. entry_type corrected boat->both (shore-accessible directly from the resort beach, 3 minutes from shore per Evolution's own site).

tags.name: Deep Slope
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: re-audited. Depth (25m) confirmed by 3 independent sources. Removed unsourced thresher-shark claim from markdown -- no source ties thresher sharks to Deep Slope specifically; that is a Monad Shoal / Kimud Shoal phenomenon tied to a deep-water cleaning station, not a feature of this shallow near-shore slope.

tags.name: Secret Wall
tags.qa_note: UNRESOLVED (deep QA 2026-08-22): no dive shop, forum, or database page could be found naming a Malapascua dive site "Secret Wall" specifically -- extensive search only returned generic west-side wall descriptions with no confirmed attribution to this name/location. Previous validated="true" tag was unsupported (source was the placeholder "dive_operator_research", not a real citation) and has been downgraded. Marine life claims in the prior markdown (pygmy seahorses, grey reef sharks, hawksbill turtles) were unsourced and have been removed. Needs human review -- possibly a locally-used nickname for a site catalogued elsewhere under a different name.

tags.name: Exotic House Reef
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: only 2 independent domains found (malapascua.net/Exotic Island's own site, padi.com) describing this site specifically -- below the 3-source bar for validated=true, so validated left as false per QA policy rather than padded. Depth (5-13m) and entry_type (shore-accessible house reef, both boat and shore) are well supported by these 2 sources and were updated. Unsourced ghost pipefish / ribbontail ray claims removed from markdown; replaced with the confirmed mandarin fish, blue-ringed octopus, and artificial-structure (sunken jeepneys/concrete) details both sources agree on.

tags.name: Lighthouse
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: re-audited. Sources conflict on depth/profile under the "Lighthouse" name -- Divebooker describes a wall to 25-30m with a deeper plateau; Kokay's and Diveplanit describe a shallow (4-12m) mandarin-fish reef at the same general location. This may be two adjacent sites sharing one name across operators. Kept existing depth (30m)/wall classification since that is what the OSM point and existing data represent, but the markdown now discloses the conflicting depth reports rather than asserting one. Removed unsourced thresher-shark claim (not supported for this site by any source found); kept the sourced seasonal hammerhead/whitetip mention (winter only, per Divebooker).

tags.name: Los Bamboos
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: confirmed as Los Bamboos Marine Sanctuary, a protected reef/training site, 5-18m depth, across 3 independent sources. Depth corrected from 20m to 18m max. Unsourced marine-life list (garden eels, burrowing gobies, wrasse, butterflyfish, parrotfish, sea turtles) removed -- no source found confirming these species at this specific site; sources instead emphasize macro/critter photography and reef-cleanup activity.

tags.name: North Point
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: reclassified pinnacle->reef (sandy/coral area, not a freestanding pinnacle) and corrected depth 35m/12m -> 24m/8m per 3 independent sources. Difficulty corrected Advanced->Intermediate (sources describe Open Water/Beginner-Intermediate suitability with variable current). REMOVED hammerhead shark claim -- dive-the-world.com explicitly states hammerheads at Malapascua are a Kimud Shoal phenomenon, not North Point; the prior markdown's hammerhead claim was an unsourced regional-species pad.

tags.name: Lapus-Lapus
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: reclassified pinnacle->reef. Three independent operator sources consistently describe Lapus-Lapus as a sloping coral reef (10-22m, commonly cited as 18m), not a freestanding pinnacle. Grey reef shark claim from prior markdown removed (unsourced); confirmed fauna (frogfish, nudibranchs, cuttlefish, mantis shrimp, sweetlips, lionfish) retained per sources.

tags.name: Lapus-Lapus 2
tags.qa_note: UNRESOLVED (deep QA 2026-08-22): only 1 independent source (oceanvibration.com, calling it "Lapus II", a 12m+ reef/wall) specifically distinguishes a second numbered Lapus-Lapus site -- below the 3-source bar, so validated left as false. Unsourced marine life (sea snakes, barracuda schools, sea turtles, 'unusual visitors') removed from markdown; replaced with an explicit no-site-specific-source note. Needs further research to confirm whether this OSM point represents a genuinely distinct site or a duplicate/alternate name for Lapus-Lapus.

tags.name: Bogtong Bato
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: re-audited, pinnacle classification and 30m depth confirmed by 3 independent sources. Resident batfish school confirmed by 2 sources (Evolution, Malapascua Thresher Shark Divers). Unsourced sea-snake and reef-shark claims removed from markdown.

tags.name: Monad Shoal
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-22: re-audited. Depth corrected 50m/5m -> 30m/16m -- the shark-viewing plateau sits at 16-30m per all sources; the 50m figure appears to have conflated the plateau with the surrounding open-water drop-off (which plunges to 200m+ but is not the dive profile). IMPORTANT: recent ScubaBoard trip reports (2025) indicate thresher shark sightings have partly shifted to nearby Kimud Shoal, with Monad Shoal encounters described as less consistent than in past years -- this is now noted in the markdown rather than presenting Monad as a guaranteed sighting. Removed unsourced hammerhead-shark and whitetip-reef-shark claims (hammerheads are attributed to Kimud Shoal specifically, not Monad, by evolution.com.ph).

tags.name: Coral Garden Marine Protected Area
tags.qa_note: UNRESOLVED (deep QA 2026-08-22): only 1 independent source (malapascua-diving.com) specifically names a "Coral Garden" site (grouped with "Cathedral" as walls/soft-coral gardens) -- below the 3-source bar, so validated left as false; previous "true" tag (sourced only to the placeholder "dive_operator_research") has been downgraded. A separately-described "Coral Gardens" snorkeling site on the west coast (oceanvibration.com) may or may not be the same location -- unclear. Unsourced napoleon wrasse / bumphead parrotfish / turtle claims removed from markdown.

tags.name: Marine Protected Area

Unsourced napoleon wrasse / bumphead parrotfish / whitetip shark claims removed from markdown; replaced with an explicit no-site-specific-source note. tags.name: Japanese Ship Wreck
tags.qa_note: UNRESOLVED (deep QA 2026-08-22, deeper wreck research per QA requirement 4): Malapascua has multiple distinct WWII Japanese wrecks and this OSM point (flagged 'location approximate') cannot be confidently matched to one. Candidates cross-checked across 2+ independent sources each: (1) Lighthouse Wreck -- a WWII Japanese landing craft, 3-7m depth, sunk by aerial bombing before reaching the beach with a cement cargo (sources: PADI, Kokay's Malapascua Diving, Dumaguete Info) -- location is close to this OSM point but depth does not match (3-7m vs recorded 17-33m). (2) Tapilon Wreck -- an unidentified WWII Japanese cargo vessel, torpedoed, now broken into several sections at 22-32m (sources: Kokay's Malapascua Diving, Dumaguete Info, Oceanvibration) -- depth is a reasonable match to the recorded 17-33m, but operators place Tapilon roughly 30 minutes offshore near the mainland town of Tapilon, inconsistent with this near-shore OSM coordinate. (3) Pioneer/Mogami Maru -- a WWII Japanese gunboat at 42-54m (multiple sources) -- too deep to match. No source gives a vessel name, build date, length, or tonnage for either plausible candidate; none is fabricated here. Do not publish wreck-history or marine-life claims until a human confirms which vessel this entry represents.
